issue.title: CMake FetchContent Examples are not working "out of the box" on MacOS and Windows when requesting https (SSL) endpoint

repository.name: cpr
repository.description: C++ Requests: Curl for People, a spiritual port of Python Requests.

issue.body:
When building the minimal cpr example using FetchContent on Windows and macOS, HTTPS (SSL) endpoints are not working. cpr responds with an `INTERNAL_ERROR` with no error message given. 

## Description
When building `cpr` with the following setup:
- CMake Build System (FetchContent minimum example)
- Clang (macOS) or MSVC (Windows)
- latest release
- SSL auto-detect (using platform-specific SSL implementation/library)
- `cpr` using "shipped/integrated" `curl`

and trying to query an HTTPS endpoint, the response indicates an INTERNAL_ERROR without a meaningful error message. I suspect the issue is within the underlying curl ssh implementation, some kind of config?

## Expected Behavior
- Minimum examples should be working without any further configuration
- `cpr` should give a meaningful error message on these internal errors
- `cpr` build should configure SSL backends correctly 

## Actual Behavior
Any request fails with `INTERNAL_ERROR`, no further message given.

## Possible Fix
Currently no suggestions, however, downgrading `cpr` to `v1.6.1` does solve all the issue. So I suspect breaking changes in `curl` which have not been fully reflected in `cpr`.

## Steps to Reproduce
Building miminum example on macOS (M1, Monterey 12.2) and Windows 10.
https://github.com/libcpr/example-cmake-fetch-content

## Context
Building minimum example shipped with `cpr`

## Your Environment
- `cpr` latest release
- Integrated/build with FetchContent CMake
- macOS (M1, Monterey 12.2) and Windows 10

body: I tracked the source of the error down to this line: https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/1669b17d3a1a1fd824308544ca0ec02a2a4f50ea/lib/vtls/x509asn1.c#L1178

I haven't tested it but it looks to me like https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/c9e0549113a2c544928d4510a2d7ef5cdabf1746 introduced the change, I think before this field with a too-big length was silently ignored?

EDIT: I'm not sure if
1) The ASN.1 parsing routine is wrong, and the length check should succeed
2) The ASN.1 parsing is correct, and the cert has bogus data. In which case
   2.1) Should the error be fixed, to correctly indicate that it's a bad certificate?
   2.2) Or should the regression be "fixed", and the length check allowed to continue, silently ignored?

issue.title: Can't send request to certain websites

repository.name: cpr
repository.description: C++ Requests: Curl for People, a spiritual port of Python Requests.

issue.body:
## Description
I am trying to perform a GET request to https://discord.com. When i send a GET request to other websites like https://www.google.com or https://httpbin.org, everything works fine. However, anything directed towards https://discord.com ends up making an internal error with no message.

## Expected Behavior
The request should be performed and return a response:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/38167139/168421476-8ffcb493-0c6c-4c60-b4c5-2915a351b9bf.png)


## Actual Behavior
The request doesn't perform, and the response object indicates that an internal error has occurred with no further information:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/38167139/168421511-3948adbf-a9fa-4464-bdb2-15461d398b08.png)


## Steps to Reproduce
Code used:
```cpp
#include "cpr/cpr.h"

int main()
{
	auto r = cpr::Get(cpr::Url{ "https://discord.com" });
	if (!r.status_code)
		std::cerr << "Error " << (int)r.error.code << " : " << r.error.message << std::endl;
	else
		std::cout << r.text << std::endl;
}
```

## Context
I'm trying to update an old API wrapper for Discord, so the code didn't change compared to what it was when it worked.

## Your Environment
* Version used: 1.8.3
* Where did you get it from: vcpkg
* Operating System and version: Windows 11 22616.100
* Link to a small example: https://github.com/JacqueSatan/ethyme.cpp/blob/master/src/client.cpp#L32

issue.title: Post request results in internal error: CURLE_OUT_OF_MEMORY

repository.name: cpr

issue.body:
<!-- Provide a general summary of the issue in the Title above -->
<!-- Use Markdown to highlight and format your code! -->
<!-- https://guides.github.com/pdfs/markdown-cheatsheet-online.pdf -->
<!-- https://developers.google.com/blockly/guides/modify/contribute/write_a_good_issue -->

## Description
<!-- Provide a more detailed introduction to the issue itself, and why you consider it to be a bug -->

When trying to make a post request to send an embed to a discord webhook the response given results in `0` with the message of `Internal Error`. Doing more digging to follow what causes the error reveals that curl is throwing `CURLE_OUT_OF_MEMORY` at some point.

## Expected Behavior
<!-- Tell us what should happen -->
Should just send embed to webhook and return `200`.

## Actual Behavior
<!-- Tell us what happens instead -->
Returns `0` with message of `Internal Error` (with evidence of actual error being `CURLE_OUT_OF_MEMORY`)

## Steps to Reproduce
<!-- Provide a link to a live example, or an unambiguous set of steps to -->
<!-- reproduce this bug. Include code to reproduce, if relevant -->
Tried sending an embed with the following code:
```cpp
cpr::Response sendWebhook(const std::string &json) {

	cpr::Body body = cpr::Body{json};
	cpr::Header header = cpr::Header{{"Content-Type", "application/json"}};
	cpr::Url url = cpr::Url{webhookURL};
	//cpr::SslOptions sslOpts = cpr::Ssl(cpr::ssl::TLSv1_3{});
	cpr::VerifySsl verifySsl = cpr::VerifySsl{false};
	cpr::Response response = cpr::Post(url, body, header, verifySsl);

	return response;
}
```

where the provided json argument was the following:
```cpp
"{\"embeds\":[{\"author\":{\"name\":\"Foxes in Love has a new post!\",\"url\":\"https://foxes-in-love.tumblr.com/post/680491087596584960\",\"icon_url\":\"https://64.media.tumblr.com/avatar_a95095bda931_512.png\"},\"image\":{\"url\":\"https://64.media.tumblr.com/9e5ee95e13e9287217978e57a5530769/d2cd88370977c72a-1f/s2048x3072/d0d6ce7affc540cb4bdbe260979b6ba9ad82acee.jpg\"}}]}"
```

and webhookURL is the URL to send the post request to (the discord webhook)  

## Context
<!-- How has this bug affected you? What were you trying to accomplish? -->
Used to use this library for fetching and posting new Tumblr posts to discord.

## Your Environment
<!-- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->
* Version used: Was just pulling from mater ([this was the most recent commit](https://github.com/libcpr/cpr/commit/5e64f82c5403f4ad0b81ec391e818699feb334c4))
* Where did you get it from (e.g. conan, vcpkg, master, ...): Master branch via CMake FetchContent
* Operating System and version: macOS 12.4
* Link to a small example: Small example provided in steps to reproduce ([here's a link to the full project if you want it though](https://github.com/yeSpud/FoxWebhook))

issue.title: Response for a HTTPS Get to Jira returns error code 4.

repository.name: cpr
repository.description: C++ Requests: Curl for People, a spiritual port of Python Requests.

issue.body:
<!-- Provide a general summary of the issue in the Title above -->
<!-- Use Markdown to highlight and format your code! -->
<!-- https://guides.github.com/pdfs/markdown-cheatsheet-online.pdf -->
<!-- https://developers.google.com/blockly/guides/modify/contribute/write_a_good_issue -->

## Description
I've been trying to do a GET request using the Jira REST API, but all that I got was an **Error Code** 4, with a **Status Code** 0

## Expected Behavior
Get the json information from the page.

## Actual Behavior
Error Code: 4
Status Code: 0
Empty Body.

## Steps to Reproduce

Here you can find two examples of what I tried.

1.
```
int main()
{
    cpr::Response response = cpr::Get(cpr::Url{ "https://mypage.atlassian.net/rest/api/latest/project" },
		cpr::Authentication{ "myuser@mydomain.com", "atlassianpasswordtoken", cpr::AuthMode::BASIC},
		cpr::Header{{"accept", "application/json"} });

    if (response.status_code == 0)
    {
        cout << response.error.message << endl; //Empty.
	cout << (int)response.error.code << endl; // 4
    }

    cout << "Url: " << response.url << endl; //https://mypage.atlassian.net/rest/api/latest/project
    cout << "Status Code: " << response.status_code << endl; // 0
    cout << "Header: " << response.header["content-type"] << endl; // Empty.
    cout << "" << response.text << endl; //Empty.

    return 0;
}
```

2.
```
int main()
{
    cpr::Url url = { "https://mypage.atlassian.net/rest/api/latest/project" };
    cpr::Authentication auth = { "myuser@mydomain.com", "atlassianpasswordtoken", cpr::AuthMode::BASIC };

    cpr::Session session;
    session.SetUrl(url);
    session.SetAuth(auth);

    cpr::Response response = session.Get();
    
    //Same responses that in the previous try.
    if (response.status_code == 0)
    {
        cout << response.error.message << endl;
        cout << (int)response.error.code << endl;
    }

    cout << "Url: " << response.url << endl;
    cout << "Status Code: " << response.status_code << endl;
    cout << "Header: " << response.header["content-type"] << endl;
    cout << "" << response.text << endl;
    
    return 0;
}
```

## Notes:
I tried different ways to do it.

- Used different url's. All of them similar, but I event tried to use just `https://mypage.atlassian.net`, expecting the html, but nothing arrived.
- Used the different values for the AuthMode.
- Encrypted the credentials.
- Tried to use the headers.
- Tried to use the parameters.

In general I did some different tests but didn't managed to get the info.

## Your Environment
<!-- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->
* Version used: 1.8.1
* Where did you get it from (e.g. conan, vcpkg, master, ...): master.
* Operating System and version: Windows 10.
